abstract: Vector clocks provide a lightweight, lock-free mechanism for capturing causal relationships in distributed systems. This work presents a pure-Python implementation that preserves the causal invariant while offering deterministic, side-effect-free operations except for explicit local increments. We formally prove that the comparison operator implements a partial order, that the increment operation preserves linearizability, and that the merge operation is associative and commutative. The algorithm achieves $O(1)$ amortized time for local updates and $O(P)$ contention-aware time for merges, where $P$ is the number of participating processes. The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_030122_vector_clock_distributed_event}.
